chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Jam sessions at the Rhythm Club
summary: Welburn steers back to 1932-36; McRae says the Rhythm Club was where musicians jammed, usually at night.

blocks.x: I see. Well before we get into -- There's a whole lot that we're going to talk about when you were with Chick Webb.
Yeah, but we're going to come back to that.

We'll come back to that. But what I'd like to do first of all is back up a bit, say, this period, the early Depression -- say 1932, '33. Very early part of 1936 -- of course, you were on and off with June Clark and Elmer Snowden, Stuff Smith and Lil Armstrong.

You were also, say, up at the Rhythm Club sometimes when you --

The Rhythm Club was a place -- Remember you asked me some time ago where did the musicians go to jam? Well, the Rhythm Club is a place where the musicians went to jam, you know, like you wasn't nothing. Different guys would come in town, you know, and have jam sessions there.
When did these jam sessions take place at the Rhythm Club?

Very seldom in the daytime. Because, if you remember, most of the guys were working and they wasn't working on jobs. They were gigging, you know, like after they come home from work, they'd go out and play.
